    Incoming multiplicity from minimal right almost-split maps #

    The total incoming-arrow multiplicity at an indecomposable endpoint is the number of indecomposable occurrences in the source of a minimal right almost-split map. Uniqueness of minimal right almost-split maps and finite Krull--Schmidt cancellation make this number independent of the chosen map and decomposition.

            If an additive functor preserves the displayed indecomposable summands and carries a minimal right almost-split map to a minimal right almost-split map, then the displayed source has the same number of occurrences as any minimal right almost-split source at the image endpoint.

            d.n ≤ bound

            If the cokernel of the anti-equivalent image of a minimal right almost-split map has a bounded minimal right almost-split source, then the original displayed source has the same bound. This is the categorical rotation used to transfer a right-mesh arity estimate through coefficient duality.
